## What this seat re-derived rather than took from the report

The saving rests on ONE property — that nothing eager reaches the validators — and a regex does not re-derive it. So it was read from the tree, not from the hand-back:

| claim | instrument | reading |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin-map` is the only live consumer in the console bundle | `git grep -n "@object-ui/types/zod" origin/main -- packages apps`, non-test | `packages/plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx:25` — the only runtime `import` inside a bundled package. `packages/cli/src/commands/{check,validate}.ts` also import it and are ⛔ not in this bundle |
| the other packages that NAME it do not import it | same output | `plugin-detail/src/index.tsx:373`, `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx:62/67`, `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx:104/109` are all **docblock prose**, ⛔ not import statements |
| ⭐ the instrument is live | the same command, counting form | the spelling occurs in dozens of files including tests and vite configs — so the short non-test list is a real subset, ⛔ not a failed search |
| the new group outranks `framework` | the diff | `types-zod` priority **82**, `framework` **80** ⇒ it claims first, which is what makes the split happen at all |
| the gate's regression scale is what the delta is judged against | `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` header | 「objectui#5266 was 89 KiB = 91,136 bytes, and this ceiling is built…」 — so 58,218 / 91,136 = **0.6388x** and 30,440 / 91,136 = **0.3340x** both check out arithmetically |

## What makes this the right shape and not the regroup objectui#9251 forbids

**Eager chunk count UNCHANGED at 329**, total chunks **+1**, eager closure **−27,776 gz / −114,892 raw**. The bytes left the closure; they did not move to another eager line. The two deltas (framework −27,778, closure −27,776) agreeing to 2 bytes is itself the check that nothing else moved.

⭐ And the find that no card could have priced: `CodeSplittingGroup.includeDependenciesRecursively` **defaults to `true`**, so the priced fix shape applied literally captures the nine validators AND absorbs `data-display.ts` / `complex.ts` / `designer.ts` — which the EAGER `plugin-grid` chunk reads through `ObjectGrid.tsx` — whereupon rolldown's higher-priority-wins rule keeps `framework` from getting them back, `plugin-grid` statically imports the new chunk, and **all 140,541 bytes stay eager**. A saving of exactly nothing wearing a new chunk name. That build is what the new guard refused, and the refusal is quoted from a real run, ⛔ not a synthetic fixture:

> `[assert-types-zod-stays-lazy] ... back in the EAGER closure: assets/types-zod-BBjRnjYY.js — statically imported by assets/plugin-grid-CB5tL5XA.js`

## ⭐ The guard's second direction is the part worth keeping

A deletion and a deferral produce the same smaller, greener number. `scripts/vite-types-zod-lazy.ts` fails the build in BOTH directions and reports the reachability half FIRST — validators dropped from the graph read as an even better saving and break the object-map view. ⛔ No byte ceiling can supply that.

The four-leg ablation ledger is what makes the guard credible rather than decorative: each leg mutated, proved the mutation landed on disk (`grep -c` of the removed text = 0), ran, restored, and proved `git diff HEAD` empty — ⛔ never by an exit code. Leg 4 is why `scripts/__tests__/check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts` is in the diff at all: its `parseGroups` required `priority` to be the LAST property, so the new group was **silently absent** from the attribution table while every case below it kept passing — 42 groups parsed, `types-zod` not among them. That is a gate that would have gone on reading green about a group it could not see.

## ⚠️ One card figure did NOT reproduce, and the dev said so instead of quietly matching it

The card priced the saving from 「27.6% of the framework chunk」, measured on objectui#9488's leg (162 modules / 509,658 rendered). On `origin/main` the chunk is 108 modules / 372,430 rendered and the same nine modules are **37.7%** of it. So the card's bracket (20,695 – 26,322 gz) does **not contain** the real figure: 27,778 is 1,456 bytes past its top, 5.5% over. ⭐ The membership claim itself reproduced exactly, and the bracket's RANKING conclusion survives untouched — the saving clears the 0.10x floor's 4,568-byte requirement by 6.1x. ⛔ But its top endpoint is not an upper bound, and a reader pricing the next chunk card off this bracket should know that.

## Two follow-ups this seat is taking, ⛔ neither folded into this PR

1. **The gate's resolution got coarser as a direct result of this change.** `PER_CHUNK_GZIP_CEILINGS.framework` (100,000) now stands 58,218 bytes — **0.6388x** the 89 KiB regression it exists to catch — above the live measurement, up from 0.3340x. Re-pinning it DOWN is the honest follow-up and the file's own header shows the precedent (「Why `framework` moved DOWN」, objectui#7399). ⛔ Correctly not taken here: the dispatch forbade touching any ceiling, baseline or exemption constant, and a re-pin is a seat/maintainer call. A card follows.
2. **objectui#9488 asserts that `packages/types` lands WHOLLY in `framework`.** After this change it is deliberately split across `framework` and `types-zod`, so whichever of the two lands second owes that assertion an update. ⛔ Not a condition on main and ⛔ not a card — it is a merge-order interaction between two open PRs, it is named in this PR's body where the lander meets it, and it is being carried into #9488's own parked decision.
